scope: Manual syntax example coverage audit; no parser/firmware verification and no example modifications.

rows.finding: E:7/22/118 demonstrate uint16, sint16 and a bounded float32 initializer. No uint8, sint32 or Q8 fixed-point declaration/initialization example in E. P:215 illustrates sint32 elsewhere; fixed-point source names remain undesigned. Numeric bounds in E use proposed `Bounds`, whereas executable F uses `Range`. Preserve that distinction pending review.

E includes initialization, literal print and boolean reassignment (18). Plain numeric variable-to-variable assignment is illustrated in C:7; sum assignment in S:7. General typed copy is not illustrated in E. Bootstrap raw bytes are a storage/interface question, not automatically a needed public intrinsic. Computed `str` printing in S remains outside Rally's implemented feature set.
E:146 demonstrates uint16 addition/reassignment. C:8 and S:7 additionally show persistent increment and two-variable addition. No new addition spelling needed.
No readable unsigned-to-containing-integer widening example found. The explicit conversion style in P/F is an existing direction, not a complete widening example.

E:118 has a float literal and bounds proposal, but no float copy, integer-to-float conversion or computation. F:2 supplies an executable bounded float declaration; P:318 illustrates integer-to-float conversion elsewhere.

P:318 shows converted operands multiplied, within a deferred imported-record example. Its math spelling can be reused independently of imports. No standalone initialized float addition/subtraction/multiplication/scaling example appears in E.
No readable scalar reciprocal/division example found. The Rally intrinsic construction is evidence of capability, not an existing friendly syntax sample.
No readable bounded constant quotient/remainder example found. Full signed/general division must not be implied by the restricted Rally operation.
F:5 and C:9 already demonstrate true floor with conversion. Reuse that syntax in E; a standalone float-valued floor result is not yet illustrated.
No readable truncation-toward-zero example found.
No readable nearest-rounding/halfway-away example found.
No readable scalar absolute-value example found.
F:5 shows the explicit signed-word conversion after floor. E does not. This can share a sample with RND-001 rather than introduce a duplicate builtin.
No readable unsigned word conversion example found. Existing uint16 declarations do not demonstrate conversion from float.
No readable bounded positive32 store/conversion example found. P's sint32 input declaration does not cover this output conversion.

P:216 illustrates a matrix declaration; P:218 initializes its value through identity/rotation. No general literal construction, typed load, extraction or cell update sample in E. Shape notation exists as a proposal; the other operations still lack examples.
No readable non-scalar matrix add/subtract/multiply/scaling sample found. P:318's scalar product does not demonstrate matrix multiplication.
P:218 illustrates identity and degree rotation. Translation, geometric scale and a composition example are not shown in E. Reuse the existing direction, keeping units and order explicit.
No readable qualified diagonal-affine inverse sample found. An arbitrary inverse would exceed Rally's proved operation.

P:224 mentions a possible point-transform wrapper in prose, but supplies no independent initialized source sample. It is a hint, not covered example syntax. Typed geometry math stays in scope; imported/indexed data and drawing stay deferred.

E:10–18 shows all six comparator symbols, boolean initialization and reassignment; E:24 adds a signed comparison. Keep these forms. Type coverage/float comparison behavior still needs semantic review, not six newly designed operators.

F:4 shows one Sub; P:253/256/259 shows two Subs and a conditional source call. E has branch bodies but no procedure declaration/call. Reuse the existing proposal; no parameters/returns or recursion implied.

E:124 shows counted For/Next; E:132 nests a conditional; E:144/153/162/171 show the four Do/Loop variants. Range/dispatch proposals also exist. No replacement loop syntax needed. A finite resident job using the existing loop/call forms can draw on P:257; backend admission restrictions are a separate issue.

E:93 tests sequence membership, not sticky runtime admission/status. H:42 describes host float validation, not a source admission builtin. No readable sticky range/equality validation example found. Copy-related admission stays deferred to GOLEM-010.

C demonstrates persistent globals and one job; H documents install/update/call/cleanup. E has no resident-job example. Share the job illustration with CTL-001/DAT-002; refer to H for transport/lifecycle instead of inventing Golem installation commands.

H:49 gives `--reserve`; ownership/layout is in generated metadata. No allocator/reservation source function is required by existing design. Keep resource configuration outside application snippets unless separately selected.
H documents artifacts/host validation. Type/shape diagnostics and maps are compiler behavior, not uncovered language functions. They do not require a new source sample per diagnostic.
Scratch sharing, pooling and inlining controls are not illustrated in E. Remain parked, consistent with the priority on wire traffic over optimization work.
Assets/tables/imports: GOLEM-010. P EX-004 is historical evidence, not authorization to expand it now.
Indexed record/element access: GOLEM-010. Switch jump-table syntax in E indexes control targets; it does not cover data indexing and does not reopen that deferred work.
Checked field/record copying: GOLEM-010. Ordinary assignment coverage does not establish checked-copy behavior.
Typed drawing: GOLEM-011. Geometry transforms above are math examples, not point/quad/bitmap/viewport rendering.
